intro_html: Dak galbi is the Korean skillet dish they cook right at your table, chicken and cabbage stir fried in gochujang until the edges char and the chewy rice cakes go soft in the middle. It is loud, red, and satisfying, and it comes together in one pan on the stovetop. Each serving lands at 564 calories and 45 grams of protein for about $6.18 a serving (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $6.18 a serving (at everyday cost). The rice cakes are the reason it is not cheaper, and they are also the reason it is dak galbi and not just spicy chicken and cabbage. That is a fair trade.
shop_smart: Korean rice cakes are far and away the biggest line on this list, more than the chicken. If you want to cut the cost hard, cut the rice cake quantity and add more cabbage, and you still have a legitimate dak galbi.
Cabbage is the cheapest vegetable in the store by volume and it is central here, not a stretcher. It wilts down and soaks up the sauce, and one head goes a very long way.
Gochujang is a several dollar tub that lasts through many batches. Between this dish and dakdoritang, it earns its shelf space fast.
Sweet potato and carrot are used in small amounts for sweetness and color. Buy a pound of each and use the rest during the week rather than letting them sit.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice cakes in warm water for 20 minutes if they came refrigerated or frozen, so they soften evenly instead of staying hard in the center.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, red pepper flakes, and black pepper with the chicken broth into a marinade.
Cut the chicken breast into bite sized pieces and toss with about half the marinade. Let it sit 20 minutes.

Cut the cabbage into wide ribbons, the sweet potato and carrot into thin slices, and the onion into wedges. Thin slices matter for the sweet potato, because it cooks slower than everything else in the pan.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet over high heat and cook the chicken until it browns at the edges, working in batches so the pan stays hot.
Add the sweet potato, carrot, onion, and drained rice cakes with the rest of the marinade and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the rice cakes soften.
Fold in the cabbage last and cook 5 more minutes, just until it wilts but still has bite. Overcooked cabbage turns watery and takes the sauce with it.
portion_html: Set the full skillet on the scale, subtract the empty weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Stir it well first, since the rice cakes sink and the cabbage floats, and one careless scoop hands somebody a container of cabbage. Every portion comes out at 564 calories.

steps: Soak the rice cakes in warm water until pliable.
Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, and pepper flakes with broth into a marinade.
Toss the cut chicken with half the marinade and rest 20 minutes.
Brown the chicken in batches in a hot skillet.
Add sweet potato, carrot, onion, rice cakes, and the rest of the marinade and cook 8 minutes.
Fold in the cabbage for 5 minutes, then weigh and divide into 14 containers.
